CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports this is approximately her 7th or 8th kidney stone. She notes the pain has been up and down. She presented to the emergency room last week and believes she passed the kidney stone approximately 3 days ago. She denies current pain or blood in the urine. She received Percocet for pain management in the emergency department. She has previously been evaluated by a urologist approximately 1 year ago. Patient also reports history of insomnia with occasional wakefulness due to worry. She has tried meditation apps which she finds helpful. She previously tried melatonin a couple of times but found it was not helpful. Regarding her diabetes, she does not check her blood sugar frequently but reports it seems to be doing pretty well.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (diagnosed approximately 1 year ago)
Recurrent kidney stones (approximately 7-8)
Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (previously documented, unchanged)
Insomnia

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports difficulty adhering to diet recommendations, consuming fast food, cakes, and cookies. She notes it is difficult to give up fast food because she is frequently on the go and has limited time for meal preparation. Sleep habits include sleeping with the television on and keeping her phone next to her bed due to concern about missing calls.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure: 150/90 mmHg
Home blood pressure readings (patient-reported, taken 2-3 times per week): 130-140/60-70 mmHg
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles
Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (previously known, no change from prior)
Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation
Costovertebral angle: No tenderness on right side

RESULTS
Prior A1C: 6.7 (from previous visit)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone: Patient appears to have passed the current stone. Ordered urinalysis and urine culture. Referral placed to urology (Dr. Harris) for evaluation and management of recurrent kidney stones.

Hypertension: Patient stable on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. Home blood pressure readings are well-controlled at 130-140/60-70 mmHg. Discussed possible white coat syndrome as elevated in-office reading of 150/90 mmHg is discordant with home readings. No medication changes. Will continue current dose with refills through pharmacy.

Diabetes: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Advised to check blood glucose before every meal.

Nutrition: Referral placed to nutrition for dietary counseling. Goal is sodium restriction to less than 2300 mg per day.

Insomnia: Continue sleep hygiene practices (electronics off, dark room, cool room). Discussed iPhone sleep mode feature to reduce interruptions. Started Melatonin 10 mg as needed for sleep.

Follow-up: Return appointment in 3 months.
